name: cavemio-toast-stack
title: Toast stack
description: Notifications that stack, fan out on hover, follow a promise in one toast, and swipe away.

cavemio.accessibility:
- Each toast is a polite status (errors are alerts), announced once as it arrives or changes. The region is labelled "Notifications (Alt+T)".
- Hovering, keyboard focus or a hidden tab pauses every timer, so nothing disappears while someone is reading it.
- Swiping works with mouse, pen and touch; vertical scrolling still passes through.
- Render one Toaster; toast() can be called from anywhere, including outside React.
- Installs Text morph. With reduced motion the toasts sit as a list and change in place.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: toast(title, options)
props.description: – · Shows a toast and returns its id. Options: description, type, duration, action { label, onClick }, id (to update one in place).

props.name: toast.success / error / info / loading
props.description: – · The same with a type, and its icon.

props.name: toast.promise(promise, messages)
props.description: – · One toast that morphs from loading to success or error. Messages can be functions of the result or error.

props.name: toast.dismiss(id?)
props.description: – · Dismiss one toast, or all of them.

props.name: Toaster position
props.description: "bottom-right" · Which corner; the stack grows away from that edge.

props.name: Toaster visible / hotkey
props.description: 3 / "t" · How many show in the stack, and the letter that, with Alt, moves focus to the newest toast.

useCases.title: Save and update feedback
useCases.description: Confirm that a change went through without a page jump.

useCases.title: Async actions
useCases.description: One toast that follows a request from start to finish.

useCases.title: Undo actions
useCases.description: A toast with an action button, such as Undo.

useCases.title: Errors
useCases.description: Tell people something failed, without a blocking dialog.

features.title: They stack neatly
features.description: A new toast rises in and the earlier ones step back into a stack, with three rims peeking out behind the newest.

features.title: They fan out on hover or focus
features.description: The stack spreads into a list at the toasts’ real heights, so every message can be read.

features.title: One toast for one request
features.description: toast.promise shows a spinner, then morphs into success with a drawn check, or into an error with a small shake.

features.title: Timers that wait for you
features.description: A thin line drains the time left and pauses while you hover, focus, or when the tab is hidden.

features.title: Swipe, close or Escape
features.description: Swipe past a threshold, press the close button or press Escape to dismiss a toast.

features.title: Callable from anywhere
features.description: Render one Toaster, then call toast() from anywhere, even outside React. Pick one of six positions. Alt+T focuses the newest.

states.title: arrive
states.description: Rises from 24px past the edge through a 4px blur with a slight overshoot (520ms); the toasts behind it scale down 5% each and step back 10px.

states.title: stacked
states.description: Up to three peek behind the newest at its height, their contents hidden; more wait out of sight.

states.title: fanned
states.description: Hover or keyboard focus spreads them into a list at their measured heights with 10px gaps; the stack’s hit area grows with it.

states.title: timer
states.description: A 1px line drains along the bottom over duration (4s by default), paused while hovered, focused or in a hidden tab; it restarts when a toast is updated.

states.title: promise
states.description: The spinner blurs into a check that draws itself (or an alert, with a 380ms shake) while the title morphs, keeping the letters the two messages share.

states.title: dismiss
states.description: Swipe past 90px (or flick) and it carries on off the edge; the close button or Escape lifts it out through a blur. The rest close up.
